blocks.text: Order tasks with dependencies compile before link, install before run. Topological sort is the algorithm that makes every build system, course scheduler, and package manager work.
A DAG(Directed Acyclic Graph) of morning tasks arrows mean "must happen before". Topological sort gives a valid order to complete them all.
You already know what a DAG is a Directed Acyclic Graph, a directed graph with no cycles.
Topological sort takes a DAG and produces a linear ordering of all its vertices such that for every directed edge A → B, vertex A comes before vertex B in the ordering.

In plain words: if task A must happen before task B, topological sort guarantees A appears first. It's the algorithm behind every build system, package manager, course prerequisite checker, and compiler.

KEY RULE:Topological sort only works on a DAG. If the graph has a cycle (A → B → C → A), there is no valid ordering you can never satisfy all the dependencies. A cycle means the problem has no solution.
Given a DAG, produce a sequence of all vertices where every edge u → v has u appearing before v. This ordering is called a topological ordering.
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406028612-729137823.png
A → B → D → F and A → C → E → F. Both are valid paths. One valid topological order: A, B, C, D, E, F
IMPORTANT: A topological ordering is not unique. Multiple valid orderings can exist for the same graph as long as every dependency comes before the node that depends on it.

There are two standard ways to compute topological sort. 
Both run in O(V + E) time. Choose based on what you need:

blocks.text: Kahn's Algorithm (BFS-based)
The intuition is simple: a node with in-degree 0 has no dependencies it can be scheduled first.
Process it, remove its outgoing edges, and see which nodes now have in-degree 0. Repeat.
IN-DEGREE EXPLAINED
In-degree of a node = number of incoming edges. A node is "ready" when its in-degree drops to 0 all its prerequisites have been completed.
In-degrees for the graph A→B, A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→F
/engineering/dsa-media/1785406029060-692341106.png
Only A starts with in-degree 0. After processing A, B and C drop to 0 and become ready next.
Kahn’s Algorithm ( Step by Step)

items:
Compute in-degrees
Count incoming edges for each node and store in inDegree[].

Add nodes with in-degree 0
Enqueue all nodes that have no incoming edges.

Dequeue and add to result
Remove a node from the queue and append it to the topological order.

Update neighbours
For each neighbour, decrease its in-degree by 1.

Add new zero in-degree nodes
If any neighbour’s in-degree becomes 0, enqueue it.

Check for cycle
If the result contains fewer than V nodes, the graph has a cycle.

blocks.text: Output:
DFS-Based Topological Sort
In DFS, when a node finishes (all its neighbours are fully explored), push it onto a stack. When DFS is complete, pop the stack that gives you the topological order.
The intuition: a node finishes only after all the nodes it points to are finished. So finishing later means coming earlier in topological order.
DFS Topological Sort Steps

items:
Run DFS from every unvisited node
Use a visited array and start DFS for each node to handle disconnected graphs.

Push after finishing DFS
After exploring all neighbours of a node, push it onto a stack.

Pop stack for result
Pop all elements from the stack to get the topological order.

Time and Space Complexity
Both algorithms visit every vertex and every edge exactly once.

blocks.text: RECOMMENDATION: For interviews, learn Kahn's algorithm first the cycle detection comes for free, and the iterative style is easier to write without bugs under pressure.

• Package managers Tools like npm, pip, and Maven install dependencies in an order that satisfies all requirements.
  • Build systems Systems like Make, Gradle, and Bazel compile files only after the files they depend on.
  • Course scheduling Take prerequisite courses before advanced ones (classic “Course Schedule” problem).
  • Task pipelines CI/CD pipelines and workflow engines execute steps in dependency order.
  • Spreadsheets Evaluate cells with formulas referencing other cells in the correct dependency order.
  • Linkers & compilers – Resolve symbol dependencies across object files and link them in the proper order.
Coming up next: Shortest Path Algorithms Dijkstra's for weighted graphs, Bellman-Ford for negative edges, and when to use each one.
